pairs.question: Dic igitur mihi, quod pulchrum nomen est puero? Quo nomine ipsum vocabimus?
pairs.derivation: Socrates' genuine question about the boy's name; Demodocus answers directly with the name. Speaker labels (So., Dem.) stripped. Self-contained interrogative with direct answer.

pairs.question: Sed tu dic mihi, Theages, cupisne sapiens esse? Ac dignum existimas esse, ut pater hic tuus virum inveniat, qui te sua consuetudine sapientem reddat?
pairs.derivation: Socrates asks Theages directly (cupisne... -ne interrogative) whether he wishes to be wise; Theages answers 'Cupio.' Speaker labels stripped. Question kept whole including the dependent clause that completes its sense; answer is the single-word direct reply.

pairs.question: Sapientes autem utrum vocas homines scientiam habentes, quaecumque illa sint quae scierint, necne?
pairs.derivation: Genuine alternative question (utrum... necne) about whom Theages calls wise; answered directly 'Scientes equidem.' Speaker labels stripped.
